newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Clinton cabinet member may face indictment-report.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Clinton cabinet member may face indictment-report.

text.p: A former member of President Clinton's cabinet has been informed that he is a target of a criminal grand jury probe and could face indictment for accepting gifts from companies he regulated, the Washington Times reported on Tuesday.

Former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy received a letter informing him of this from independent counsel Donald Smaltz, who has conducted an investigation for nearly three years into allegations that Espy accepted favours from poultry and meat companies, the newspaper said.
A spokesman for Smaltz could not immediately be reached for comment. Espy's attorney also was unavailable.
The independent counsel's office previously indicated it hoped to finish the lengthy investigation this summer.
Espy, a former congressman from Mississippi, resigned from his cabinet post in 1994. He has denied any wrongdoing.
Last month, poultry giant Tyson Foods Inc. said it expected to be indicted in what it described as a "misguided" investigation.
So far in the Espy probe, the independent counsel has won convictions against three corporations, five individuals and one law firm, and won $3.5 million in fines.
But a lobbyist for Tyson Foods, Jack Williams, was granted a new trial this summer after a federal judge found that prosecutors failed to reveal that an FBI agent witness had lied in another case.
